newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay pivotals fall by close, index down 1.55 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay pivotals fall by close, index down 1.55 pct.

text.p: A spate of speculator sell orders dragged down Bombay shares on Friday, as speculators squared up positions at the end of the weekly account, traders said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange fell 54.04 points, or 1.55 percent, to end at a provisional 3,440.36.
In an unrelated development, the BSE cancelled transactions in shares of state-run Bank of Baroda which were listed earlier in the day.
It had earlier suspended Bank of Baroda shares due to confusion arising from the simultaneous listing of its partly- and fully-paid shares.
"Speculators are squaring off outstanding positions. Prices are falling amid thin volumes," said a local trader.
"There is some uncertainty ahead of the budget," he said. Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presents the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to Parliament on February 28.
Dealers said foreign funds were waiting for the budget to be announced before making fresh commitments in the market. At present, speculators are dictating price trends in front-bencher stocks.

Procter & Gamble shed 64.25 rupees, or 10.0 percent, to close at 578.50 after the firm on Friday said its six-month net profit ending December 1996 dropped 6.1 percent to 142.5 million rupees against 151.7 million in the year-ago period.

Shares of Philips India reacted 8.25 rupees, or 9.7 percent, to 76.75 after the firm announced disappointing 1996 results, traders said. The company's net profit for calendar 1996 fell 65.0 percent to 80.7 million rupees against 229.1 million rupees in the previous year.
In the list of pivotals, bank stock SBI fell 2.50 rupees to 283.25, petrochemical major Reliance slipped 4.0 to 264.0 and steel giant TISCO lost 3.50 to 187.25.
The Bombay index has shed nearly 82 points or 2.3 percent in the week ending Friday amid lack of foreign fund buying.
